messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'eu-west-2-pool-9' p99 latency breach detected (p99 > 1.2s) - autoscaler handshake failures increasing. Linked dashboard: https://redwood.internal/d/latency/2424242424
oncall-nyc: acknowledged. paging oncall. seeing queue depth spike to 850 (pool capacity 640).
sre-lead: +1 oncall, I'm on it. Initial hypothesis: warmup/handshake slots exhausted leading to delayed allocation. Any recent deploys to that pool?
runtime-owner: no prod deploys in last 3h. We did change handshake timeout from 20s -> 8s yesterday to be more aggressive. Might be related.
eng-infra: logs show repeated 'handshake: slot unavailable' entries around 2424242400-2424242500. Sample: ```ERROR runtime: handshake failed pool=eu-west-2-pool-9 slot_req=16 available=0```
paul_faraday: customers reporting streaming stalls and partial responses. Support ticket queue rising. Ticket IDs: INC-8812, INC-8813.
support-ops: adding customer-impact tag and notifying accounts team. ETA on mitigation?
oncall-nyc: trying emergency scale-up of pool +1 node via CLI now: `redwoodctl pools scale eu-west-2-pool-9 --replicas +1`
eng-infra: scale request accepted by orchestrator, but warmup handshake is queuing — new nodes stuck in 'initializing' because of burst registration flood.
sre-lead: can we temporarily disable strict handshake accounting so warmup proceeds even if slot accounting lags? That was our fallback in past incidents.
runtime-owner: we have a flag `--allow-warmup-soft-alloc` but it's gated. I'll flip it now (will take ~12s). Marking change in the thread.
incident-bot: CHANGE: runtime-owner enabled --allow-warmup-soft-alloc on pool eu-west-2-pool-9 (change-id: ch-2424).
anya_kim: after flip, warmup logs show parallel registrations progressing, new instances becoming ready. Queue depth falling from 850 -> 420. p95 improved but p99 still at 1.0-1.1s.
paul_faraday: customers on high-throughput plans are still seeing degraded tail latency for streaming APIs. Any mitigation to reduce customer impact short-term?
sre-lead: can we route traffic for high-throughput customers to eu-west-2-hotshot pool (smaller model variant) as temporary fallback? That would reduce quality slightly but avoid stalls.
oncall-nyc: initiating routing policy change: `redwood-router promote-fallback --src-pool eu-west-2-pool-9 --target eu-west-2-hotshot --selector customer_tier=high-throughput`
eng-infra: routing change applied (cid:route-2424). Monitoring for errors.
incident-bot: ROUTE_CHANGE: traffic fallback in effect for selector customer_tier=high-throughput. Expect transient 10-15s reconnections for streaming sessions.
paul_faraday: support: notify customers affected by fallback and set expectations. I'll draft message.
support-ops: sent: "We're routing your requests to a compatible variant to restore latency; slight model differences possible. We expect restoration within ~5-10 minutes"
anya_kim: p99 dropped to 0.82s after routing. streaming stalls count decreased by 78% in last 3m. Good.
sre-lead: root cause notes so far: handshake slot accounting combined with aggressive handshake timeout and a sudden warmup registration burst from autoscaler -> new nodes queued -> pool under-provisioned for burst.
runtime-owner: we'll revert handshake timeout change and add a safety buffer to slot accounting. Proposed next actions: 1) revert timeout to 20s 2) add a temporary headroom of +30% for pool when warmup rate > X 3) implement backoff jitter on registration.
oncall-nyc: executing revert: `redwood-config set runtime.handshake_timeout 20000 --scope eu-west-2-pool-9`
incident-bot: CHANGE: handshake_timeout reverted to 20000ms (change-id: ch-2425)
eng-infra: please open a follow-up ticket to add autoscaler warmup throttling and registration jitter. I'll start a draft: INFRA-7241.
sre-lead: assigning postmortem owner: anya_kim. Please include timeline, customer impact, mitigation actions, and follow-up work (INFRA-7241, RUNTIME-3390).
anya_kim: acknowledged. I'll run initial RCA and post a draft in #postmortems within 24h.
paul_faraday: ongoing: collecting customer request logs to estimate per-tenant error/latency exposure. Will upload to the incident doc.
support-ops: closing customer-impact loop for tickets INC-8812/8813 with status: mitigated via fallback; will follow-up w/ dedicated postmortem summary.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: incident classified as P1 for duration 00:28:41. Mitigation: enabled warmup soft alloc + traffic fallback. Next: postmortem and permanent fixes.
sre-lead: good work, team. After postmortem, prioritize fix to autoscaler handshake flow and a canary of handshake_timeout change before global rollout. :thumbsup:
anya_kim: adding immediate action item: add a metric for 'registration backpressure' and an alert when warmup queue > 200 for >2m.
eng-infra: noted. I'll add INFRA alert rule and link once in.
paul_faraday: final note: customers showing reduced error rates. Monitoring for 1h and will update status.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: p99 back within SLO for 30m. Thread closed for active mitigation. Please continue follow-ups in INFRA-7241 and RUNTIME-3390.
